data.gender_notes: Lalitkant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Lalitkant is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Lalita' meaning 'playful', 'light' or 'movement' and 'Kant' meaning 'power'. In Hindu mythology, Lalitkant is an aspect of Lord Vishnu, symbolizing the divine power of creation, preservation, and destruction. The name Lalitkant carries the meaning “Light, Movement” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lalitkant usually hope their child will grow to embody light, movement and live with faith, good character and purpose.

vedic_reference.note: Lalitkant is a name derived from the Vedic Goddess Lajjā, who is known for her kindness, grace, and beauty. She is also the wife of Vishnu, and is believed to grant her devotees' desires. The name Lalitkant is a combination of Lajjā (easily pleased) and Kant (God), reflecting the divine qualities of being kind, graceful, and godly.

historical_references.reference: Lalitkant was a renowned Jain scholar and poet, born in the 12th century in present-day Gujarat. He is best known for his work 'Vadinam Sutra' which is a commentary on the 'Agama Sutra'. This work is considered an important text in Jain philosophy and scripture.

Another significant work of Lalitkant is 'Dasavimshatika', a commentary on the 'Nataka Ratna' of the Jain philosopher Hemacandra. This work is a major contribution to Jain aesthetics and theatre studies.
